text.p: Operators of the Channel Tunnel held a "satisfactory" emergency drill on Sunday in an attempt to persuade safety authorities to allow them to reopen the subsea link to passenger rail services after last month's fire.
Some 650 "passengers" were evacuated from the tunnel successfully after a simulated accident, a Eurotunnel Plc SA spokeswoman said.
The passengers, mostly Eurotunnel staff and families, were evacuated within two hours and 10 minutes.
"It was satsfactory, it went as planned and it is now up to the safety authority to make up their minds," spokeswoman Sarah Griffiths told Reuters.
Some freight trains are already passing through the tunnel and the safety authority must now decide whether it can be re-opened to passenger services.
Eurotunnel Managing Director Alain Bertrand said: "We hope for an early resumption of passenger services."
The Channel tunnel safety authority is expected to meet this week to decide whether or not to approve the re-opening of the fire-damaged tunnel.
But a local British member of parliament criticised the safety drill, saying it had been conducted under unrealistic conditions.
MP Roger Gale said: "If it took two hours to get everyone out and 20 minutes for passengers to walk through the service tunnel, that is unsatisfactory."
